summary: Recorded SPEC-02 deviation upheld: worked by hand (3 seats, button 1; preflop 1 calls 4, 2 completes, 3 checks; flop 2 bets 4, 3 raises 8, 1 raises 12, 2 raises 16) seat 3 has 8 in and owes 8 on the flop; on the turn/river (8/16/24/32) seat 3 has 16 in and owes 16. This matches spec section 5's turn example ([fold, call 16]) and the call = min(owed, stack) rule; the prose '12 / 24' in SPEC-02 is a spec error (those would be the amounts owed by seat 1, not the next seat). Raise-one-unit-higher amounts (20 flop, 40 turn/river) are correct. Engine cap is a single clause in legalActions applying to all streets and table sizes (heads-up covered preflop and flop; 2-10 sizes covered by the 100k run); stack check is unchanged and short all-in raises are left to TASK-1.14. invariants.ts is untouched and does not import STREET_BET_CAP (also asserted by test). fifthBet fixture matches spec A-4 verbatim; locked TASK-1.8 invariants acceptance test is unchanged and passes; runner unit test now asserts betCount 3 consistent with the fixture. D-3 edit in the locked chip-safety test is exactly one line (createHand stake), no assertion changes. Tests would fail if the cap were removed (expectCapped toEqual exact [fold, call], AC#4 overCap and checker violations), if the policy regained a betCount filter (synthetic-raise draw), or if the advice clause dropped the engine constant. Targeted suites run locally: 12 files, 52 tests passed. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
